What comes up in Kiama

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. Treat the rows as the usual shape of the job locally. A specific property can differ, and that is what a site visit settles.

Rural property clearance

Sheds, stables, fencing, concrete and vegetation on a holding that is being rebuilt or subdivided.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials assessed and removed first, then the structures and vegetation off by stream, with retained plantings protected.
What does it
Large excavator with a grapple, mulcher where the volume suits it, truck and dogs.

Coastal dwelling on a village block

Older housing close to the centre, with neighbours near and limited street room.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, then careful demolition with the neighbouring structures protected and loads sequenced against the machine.
What does it
Midi excavator, tippers at the kerb.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Kiama

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Coastal and rural blocks side by side A village centre, coastal housing and farmland within a short distance.
  • Significant plantings On many properties, where tree approval becomes the longest item on a clearing programme.
  • Rural outbuildings Sheds, stables and farm structures where weathered fibro is common.
  • The longest haul on the corridor Distance to a licensed facility is a real part of the price here and is set by the classification.

Kiama properties generally have room and the rural blocks take any plant, but the haul is long and that shapes the economics more than the access does. On the coastal blocks the usual narrow street constraints apply.

Kiama questions

What people ask before we start

Is it economic to bring you this far?
Sometimes yes and sometimes no, and we will say which. Travel is accounted for honestly in the quote rather than hidden in the rates, and where a job does not stack up we would rather tell you than price it and hope.
There are large trees on the property. What happens?
Tree removal depends on approval rather than on plant, and it is worth starting that process well before the work is programmed. Retained trees keep their root zones clear of machines and stockpiles.
What happens if the fill turns out to be contaminated?
It is tested and classified before it moves, then taken to a facility licensed to receive that classification. Given the industrial history around Wollongong this is a real possibility rather than a remote one, and remediation can sit on the same contract.
Who actually removes the asbestos?
Licensed asbestos removalists do the removal. Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and builds the programme around them, and an independent licensed assessor handles the air monitoring and the clearance. You are dealing with one contract rather than three.
